purpose: Test two new branches without collapsing speculation into evidence: (A) whether repeated Egyptian gold phallic sheaths/amulets could share a workshop template or mandrel, and (B) whether a female-genital/fertility object branch changes the Osiris/Seth search graph.

branch_A_template_test.hypothesis: Some gold phallic funerary objects may have been produced from reusable workshop forms, mandrels or templates.
what_would_support_shared_tooling: same 3D geometry after scale-normalization and in absolute dimensions
matching edge finishing and foil thickness
repeated tool or die marks in homologous positions
matching construction sequence visible by microscopy or radiography
branch_A_template_test.critical_inference_limit: Even a proven common mandrel would estimate a workshop standard, not the anatomical size of Osiris. To infer a divine original, an independent text/object would have to state that the form was copied directly from the relic.

comparison_corpus.context: Mendes 1902 burial of Nesbanebdjedet; human funerary equipment; owner independently attested as Prophet of Osiris in Anpet.
Morimoto 1989 reports a gilded resin penis-and-scrotum model placed below intact male genitalia in an Egyptian mummy.

branch_B_female_genital_control.hypothesis: Search bias toward phallic objects may miss female-genital or fertility-symbol objects that occupy equivalent ritual/protective roles.
source_bound_controls: The Met states Egyptian cowries were valued partly because of resemblance to the female vulva and fertility association.
UCL and Brooklyn document Egyptian female fertility figures with explicit pubic triangles/genital emphasis.
British Museum documents mold-made Ptolemaic naked pregnant female fertility amulets.
ROM notes gold protective body covers were used for mummies of both men and women in Ptolemaic/Roman Egypt.
branch_B_female_genital_control.search_consequence: Mirror the Mendes/Osiris catalog pass with female-genital/fertility classes, especially small gold/shell/amuletic objects and body-covering components from the same archaeological contexts.

evidence: UCL creation synthesis presents Osiris and Seth as sons/male gods and Isis/Nephthys as goddesses.
Book of the Dead 42 explicitly identifies the phallus with Osiris and the back with Seth.

Egyptian myth does permit sexually complex role reversals: Horus/Seth narratives include semen transfer and Seth receiving Horus's semen, but this does not establish female anatomy or female identity.
Female rulership in historical Egypt demonstrates political gender complexity, not that Osiris or Seth were secretly women.

important_material_control.description: Ptolemaic Osiris statuette in Vienna has penis and testicles formed separately and inserted into an oval recess; the figure had been linen-wrapped and contained 12 amulets within the mummy wrapping.
important_material_control.interpretation: A detachable/artificial Osirian phallus is materially real at the level of ritual statuary. This supports testing modular phallus construction and attachment failure as an object-history question, but does not show that a detached ceremonial phallus generated the ancient myth.

new_gates.goal: Collect exact dimensions, foil thickness, seam/fold geometry, tool marks and manufacturing technique for Mendes 1902 gold phallus sheath plus JE 56935, JE 56967 and other secure Egyptian comparanda; compare only like-for-like construction classes.
Repeat the Mendes provenance sweep for vulva/cowrie/pubis/fertility/female-body-cover objects, preserving their exact archaeological context and avoiding modern projection.

Catalogue Osiris figures with separately made/inserted phalli, attachment sockets, repairs or missing genital inserts; determine whether modular construction is widespread and whether any examples preserve workshop-standard dimensions.
